title: Saints Joachim and Anne
short_summary: Saints Joachim and Anne are venerated in Catholic tradition as the parents of the Blessed Virgin Mary and the grandparents of Jesus, though their names come from early non-canonical tradition.
key_facts: In the 2026 U.S. calendar, July 26 is the Seventeenth Sunday in Ordinary Time.
They are honored as the parents of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
The canonical Gospels do not name Mary's parents.
Traditional details about their lives come from apocryphal sources and should be handled carefully.

sections.heading: Mary's parents in tradition
sections.body: Catholic tradition venerates Joachim and Anne as the parents of the Blessed Virgin Mary. Their place in devotion points to the real human family into which Mary was born and through which God prepared, in hidden providence, for the Incarnation.

sections.heading: What is certain and what is not
sections.body: The Church honors them as saints, but the canonical Gospels do not provide their names or life details. Many familiar stories come from early non-canonical writings and later devotion.

sections.heading: Grandparents of the Lord
sections.body: Their memorial helps Catholics remember that salvation history passes through families, generations, and hidden fidelity, while keeping the focus on Christ and his Mother.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Family and providence
catholic_connection_sections.body: Joachim and Anne point to God's providence working through ordinary family life and generations of faith.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Careful tradition
catholic_connection_sections.body: Catholic devotion can honor tradition without treating every later story as certain history.

historical_cautions: The names and many life details of Joachim and Anne come from apocryphal tradition rather than the canonical Gospels.
Do not present apocryphal stories about them as certain historical facts.
